screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of a systemic immunomodulator (inosiplex) in alopecia totalis; meets RCT criterion evaluating a systemic intervention in AA/AT/AU.
Randomized, placebo-controlled trial of oral prednisolone (systemic) in extensive alopecia areata; clearly an RCT evaluating a systemic intervention.
Multicenter, prospective, randomized, controlled, investigator-blinded trial comparing two topical corticosteroids in mild-to-moderate alopecia areata; RCT of a topical intervention.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized evaluation of topical minoxidil in extensive alopecia areata/totalis/universalis; RCT topical intervention.
Double-blind assignment to topical minoxidil vs placebo (then crossover to minoxidil), evaluating effectiveness in extensive alopecia areata; RCT topical intervention (at least in initial phase).
Randomized, double-blind half-head design testing DPCP with either topical 5% minoxidil or vehicle; RCT of topical adjunctive intervention in severe alopecia areata.

Patients with alopecia totalis/universalis nonresponders were randomly assigned to topical cyclosporine, PUVA, or intravenous thymopentin; randomized comparative trial including systemic and topical arms.
Small within-subject study of topical photodynamic therapy with multiple concentrations and vehicle on different scalp areas; randomization not stated and design does not clearly constitute an RCT.
Randomized comparison of topical cyclosporin A versus vehicle in therapy-refractory alopecia areata; RCT of a topical intervention.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled study of systemic imipramine in alopecia areata; RCT of a systemic intervention.

Thirty patients with severe recalcitrant AA randomly assigned to topical immunotherapy, systemic interferon alpha, or the combination; randomized controlled design including systemic and topical interventions.

Double-blind study comparing topical cyclosporin A vs placebo in alopecia areata; although randomization is not explicitly stated, double-blind placebo-controlled topical comparisons are typically randomized; include conservatively.
Randomized, double-blind, right–left, placebo-controlled trial of topical clobetasol foam in moderate to severe alopecia areata; RCT topical intervention.
Randomized controlled trial: all received systemic prednisone taper, then randomized to 2% topical minoxidil vs vehicle; evaluates effectiveness of topical adjunct following systemic steroids; RCT.

Report includes a double-blind, placebo-controlled study of topical minoxidil in extensive alopecia areata (among broader program); RCT component present though abstract is mixed; include conservatively for title/abstract screening.

Controlled trial on 119 patients comparing squaric acid dibutylester, diphencyprone, minoxidil, and placebo for patchy AA; randomization not explicitly stated, but a multi-arm controlled comparison with placebo likely randomized; include conservatively.
Questionnaire study on illness perceptions in alopecia areata; not a randomized controlled trial of an intervention.
Methodological commentary on when randomized trials are unnecessary; not an RCT in alopecia areata.
Randomized, double-blind, controlled trial of aromatherapy (topical essential oils) for alopecia areata; RCT topical intervention.
Narrative update/review on alopecia areata; not a randomized controlled trial.
Population-based incidence/natural history study; not a randomized controlled trial of an intervention.
Observational analysis of prognostic factors in patients treated with DPCP; no randomized controlled design.
Three-arm comparison in alopecia totalis with groups matched for age/sex; randomization not stated and appears nonrandomized; does not meet RCT criterion.
Genetics review; not a randomized controlled trial.
Methodological paper on trial quality; not an RCT in alopecia areata.
